Homography Camera Location Experiment

True yaw is intentionally held constant. The transformed image simulates camera location change using each sample's positive pitch value and the homography camera-location effect, then the trained model is used to compare old and new yaw predictions. Aggregate plots use all rows; the image viewer shows 1000 of 1000 rows.

Transform Method

This page studies a projective homography-style transform for camera location change. Unlike affine warping, the top and bottom rows can scale differently, so parallel image structure may converge. The current dashboard can use either discrete pitch values or a continuous positive range such as +10 to +15 degrees.

normalized row: y_n = y / (H - 1)
strength: s = clamp(deg, 0, 20) / 10
projective denominator: d(y) = 1 + 0.075 s (0.5 - y_n)
row scale: scale(y) = 1 - 0.065 s (1 - y_n)
source x: x_s = c_x + (x - c_x) / (scale(y) d(y))
source y: y_s = y + 1.35 s (1 - y_n) / d(y)

Because this experiment tests visual robustness to apparent camera location changes, the transformed image is treated as a domain perturbation and the yaw label remains unchanged.
